findings.issue_text: Default max_processes=None silently spawns one flusher process per shard on all instantiation paths except the ingest-spans CLI entry, changing production behavior without tests and disagreeing with the CLI option default of 1
join() shutdown timeout is consumed serially by the first process, so remaining processes are terminated before flushing buffered segments when num_processes > 1
submit() record_stored_segments() Redis round-trips (and get_memory_info() calls) are multiplied by process count on every poll cycle, a hot-path regression
Inconsistent metric tag keys 'shard' vs 'shards' split the same series across two tag names, causing incomplete dashboard data for wait_produce
Hung flusher threads in the produce_to_pipe path are 'restarted' by spawning a replacement thread while the hung one keeps running and double-polls the same shards
test_flusher_processes_limit asserts internal attributes but never verifies flushing behavior through the 2 processes, leaving the multiplexing/demultiplexing logic uncovered
_create_process_for_shard is dead code with a latent bug: it recreates a process without terminating the old one and is never called in the diff

Metric tag-name inconsistency: wait_produce timer uses tag key "shards" while flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes use "shard" and flusher_unhealthy uses "shard" with an integer value, causing dashboards/alerts keyed on "shard" to drop wait_produce latency data and preventing cross-flush-lifecycle aggregation
In join(), the deadline-exhaustion break exits the outer per-process loop, skipping process.terminate() for processes not yet reached, leaking live processes/threads on slow shutdown

Default divergence for max_processes: factory default (None) yields one process per shard while CLI default is one process total, and `max_processes or len(...)` swallows flusher_processes=0 and lets negative values crash with KeyError instead of a config validation error
Metric shard_tag is a comma-joined shard list rather than a single shard, so per-shard dashboards never match, cardinality grows with assignment permutations, and aggregation by shard is impossible
_create_process_for_shards restart path replaces self.buffers[process_index] with a new SpansBuffer without closing the old one, leaking Redis connection pools on repeated crash-restarts
_create_process_for_shard is dead code never called anywhere in the diff, a change-safety trap from an incomplete refactor

Bare time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a fixed-wait race bandaid that can flake on slow CI runners

In thread mode, hang restart never stops the old hung thread since process.kill() is guarded by isinstance check, leaking a thread and running duplicate pollers on the same shards (P2)

submit() performs one record_stored_segments() Redis round-trip per process-buffer instead of one, multiplying Redis calls N× with per-shard default; get_memory_info also double-counts used/available N times (P2)

Metric tag key drift: timers use tag 'shard' while wait_produce uses 'shards', splitting one logical metric family across two tag keys and breaking dashboards/alerts

Per-process backpressure semantics have defects
Restart-counter behavior is incorrect
`join` deadline handling is problematic
Removed `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call replaced by per-shard buffers raises correctness/architecture concerns

_ensure_processes_alive health monitoring logic has zero test coverage: no test kills a process, manipulates process_healthy_since, or drives the restart loop (including MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, kill/already-closed path, and restart via _create_process_for_shards)

join() lets the first slow process consume the entire shared deadline, breaking the outer loop and leaving remaining processes neither joined nor terminate()d (leaked processes holding Redis connections); no test calls join with a timeout on a multi-process flusher

Weakened assertion at test_flusher.py:83 uses any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values()), which passes if any process is in backpressure rather than the specific tested process, masking per-process backpressure state
submit() backpressure semantics changed (raises MessageRejected if any per-process value exceeds threshold), but no test verifies that submit raises MessageRejected after the threshold elapses

Killed/replaced processes are never join()ed in _ensure_processes_alive, accumulating zombie SpawnProcess entries (holding pickled SpansBuffer/pipe resources) across repeated crash-restart cycles

_create_process_for_shard is a dead method with a misleading contract — it restarts an entire process group rather than one shard and has no callers
flusher_processes=0 (or negative) silently means one process per shard (the maximum) instead of an error, inverting the intent of operators setting 0

Per-message Redis call amplification in flusher submit(): loop issues one Redis round-trip set per flusher process, plus get_memory_info() per buffer when max-memory-percentage < 1.0, all on the consumer's hot ingest path; with N processes this multiplies synchronous Redis traffic and can itself trigger MessageRejected under backpressure

Empty assigned_shards at construction makes num_processes 0, silently disabling the flusher entirely: no process polls Redis, spans rot in Redis while offsets are still committed, with no error surfaced

_create_process_for_shard is a dead-but-dangerous restart helper that doesn't kill the old process, doesn't increment process_restarts, and bypasses the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS check, risking zombie processes and unbounded restart loops if wired in

Inconsistent metric tag key for the same dimension: 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' uses tag 'shard' while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' uses 'shards', splitting dashboards/alerts into disjoint series and breaking series continuity

shard_tag joins all shard ids into a comma-separated metric tag value (e.g. '0,1,2,...,63') when one process covers many shards, causing metric cardinality blowup and making per-shard breakdowns structurally impossible

--flusher-processes 0 (or falsy value) is silently converted via `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` to one process per shard (the maximum) rather than being rejected or clamped, causing silent maximal process fan-out

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default max_processes=None silently spawns one flusher process per shard on all instantiation paths except the ingest-spans CLI entry, changing production behavior without tests and disagreeing with the CLI option default of 1

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes SpanFlusher default to `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (in `flusher.py`), which results in `num_processes == len(assigned_shards)` (one process per shard) when `max_processes` is not provided. Separately, the ingest-spans CLI wiring adds a `--flusher-processes` click option with `default=1` (`consumers/__init__.py`), which would drive `max_processes=1` via `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(flusher_processes=...)` (`factory.py`). That’s a concrete default mismatch and can change runtime resource usage depending on how the factory is instantiated. There is a test for the limit case, but no test asserting/guarding the new default behavior, and the inconsistency itself is a review-worthy issue even if intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() shutdown timeout is consumed serially by the first process, so remaining processes are terminated before flushing buffered segments when num_processes > 1

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), a single global deadline is used while iterating processes, but the code does not terminate “remaining processes” after the first one consumes the timeout. If the deadline is exceeded, it `break`s out of the loop before reaching later processes, meaning they are neither waited on nor terminated (they may keep running with `stopped` set). Thus the specific claim that remaining processes are terminated before flushing due to serial timeout consumption is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() record_stored_segments() Redis round-trips (and get_memory_info() calls) are multiplied by process count on every poll cycle, a hot-path regression

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit(), the diff changes from a single buffer call to iterating over all per-process buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and similarly aggregates memory info across all buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`). Previously these were single calls on `self.buffer`. This makes Redis/memory-info work scale with `num_processes` for every `submit()` invocation, which is a concrete performance/regression concern introduced by the change, though not a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag keys 'shard' vs 'shards' split the same series across two tag names, causing incomplete dashboard data for wait_produce
Hung flusher threads in the produce_to_pipe path are 'restarted' by spawning a replacement thread while the hung one keeps running and double-polls the same shards

adjudication.rationale: In the `produce_to_pipe` path, `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`) (see `make_process = threading.Thread`). When `_ensure_processes_alive` detects a hang via `time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`, it attempts to restart by calling `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, but it only kills the old worker if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Threads are not stopped/terminated/joined, so the old hung thread can remain alive while a replacement thread is started for the same shard set, leading to multiple threads polling/producing for the same shards. The dict entry is overwritten, but the original thread keeps running.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit asserts internal attributes but never verifies flushing behavior through the 2 processes, leaving the multiplexing/demultiplexing logic uncovered

adjudication.rationale: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only inspects internal state (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and `process_to_shards_map`) and then immediately calls `step.join()` without submitting any messages or asserting that spans are actually flushed/produced. Additionally, because `produce_to_pipe=messages.append` is provided, the flusher uses `threading.Thread` (not `mp_context.Process`), so the test does not exercise the multiprocessing path or validate that the shard-to-process multiplexing/demultiplexing logic affects real flushing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code with a latent bug: it recreates a process without terminating the old one and is never called in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard` but nothing in the shown changes calls it (the code paths use `_create_processes()`, `_create_process_for_shards()`, and restarts happen in `_ensure_processes_alive()`), so it is dead code in this PR. The method also recreates a process via `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without terminating/killing the existing process first (unlike `_ensure_processes_alive()`, which attempts to kill before restarting), which would be a latent process-leak bug if it were ever invoked. As-is, it’s a real diff-grounded cleanup/maintenance issue rather than a verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default divergence for max_processes: factory default (None) yields one process per shard while CLI default is one process total, and `max_processes or len(...)` swallows flusher_processes=0 and lets negative values crash with KeyError instead of a config validation error

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` plumbing but does no validation and uses `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` in `SpanFlusher.__init__`. This (a) makes `flusher_processes=0` behave like “unset” (falls back to `len(assigned_shards)`), and (b) allows negative values to reach `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))`, producing `num_processes < 0`, an empty `process_to_shards_map`, and then a `KeyError` during shard assignment (`self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`). Also, the CLI default is explicitly `default=1` while the factory default `None` yields one process per shard (via the `or len(...)` fallback), a real behavioral divergence visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric shard_tag is a comma-joined shard list rather than a single shard, so per-shard dashboards never match, cardinality grows with assignment permutations, and aggregation by shard is impossible

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, `shard_tag` is set to a comma-joined list of all shards handled by that process (`shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`) and then used in metric tags like `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`. This makes the `shard` tag value represent a shard *set* (e.g. "0,2") rather than a single shard id, which can explode metric cardinality as shard assignments vary and prevents straightforward per-shard aggregation/filtering. The diff also inconsistently uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` for `wait_produce`, further fragmenting dashboards/queries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shards restart path replaces self.buffers[process_index] with a new SpansBuffer without closing the old one, leaking Redis connection pools on repeated crash-restarts

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, each restart creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` and then overwrites `self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer` without any explicit cleanup of the previous buffer for that process index. The diff does not show whether `SpansBuffer` owns/needs explicit closing of Redis connections/pools, so the specific claim about “leaking Redis connection pools” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the restart path clearly lacks any teardown for the old buffer instance and is a concrete resource-lifecycle concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code never called anywhere in the diff, a change-safety trap from an incomplete refactor

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the new helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` is introduced but there is no call site shown in the diff. The refactor uses `_create_processes()` / `_create_process_for_shards(...)` for startup and `_ensure_processes_alive()` restarts processes via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, never the per-shard variant. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` dead code in the presented changes and could mislead future edits as if shard-level restarts exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weakened test verification: assert any(x.value ...) only checks at least one process saw backpressure, masking regression class where a process's backpressure signal is dropped after the per-process split

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the flusher from a single backpressure flag (`backpressure_since`) to per-process flags (`process_backpressure_since`), and the test assertion is correspondingly weakened from checking a single value to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`. This does reduce what the test guarantees (it no longer verifies that the specific expected process/shards saw backpressure, nor that all relevant processes did), so it could miss some classes of per-process signaling regressions. However, the diff alone doesn’t establish that *all* processes should show backpressure in that test scenario, so this is a test coverage/precision concern rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zero test coverage for three new non-trivial behaviors: multi-process restart with MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError path, join() multi-process shutdown/timeout logic, and multi-process submit() backpressure aggregation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new multi-process logic in `SpanFlusher`: per-process restart tracking and the `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError path in `_ensure_processes_alive`, multi-process shutdown/wait/terminate logic in `join()`, and aggregated backpressure rejection in `submit()` by iterating `process_backpressure_since.values()`. The added tests only cover process-count limiting and shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and a minimal backpressure assertion change (`assert any(...)`), but do not exercise restart escalation/RuntimeError, join timeout/partial shutdown behavior, or the “any process backpressured long enough causes MessageRejected” aggregation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flaky test: time.sleep(0.1) as sole synchronization in test_consumer.py:60-63 can cause ValueError on unpacking messages on slow CI runners

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the added synchronization is `time.sleep(0.1)` after `step.poll()` (lines shown around the new block before `step.join()`), but earlier the test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so this sleep is a no-op. That means the test is still effectively relying on thread/process scheduling for the flusher to produce into `messages` before `step.join()`, and `(msg,) = messages` will raise `ValueError` if `messages` is still empty on a slow/contended runner. The diff therefore introduces/keeps a real flakiness risk grounded in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests exercise only the threading.Thread path while production runs the spawn process path, leaving the pickling of newly constructed per-shard SpansBuffer untested, risking production-only startup crash

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes the flusher create per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances and, when `produce_to_pipe is None`, starts a `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process` with `partial(SpanFlusher.main, shard_buffer)` (i.e., `shard_buffer` must be pickled for the child). However, the added/updated tests instantiate `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=messages.append)`, which forces the `threading.Thread` path in `_create_process_for_shards` and avoids any pickling. So the spawn/process startup path (and pickling of the per-shard `SpansBuffer`) is not exercised by tests, creating a concrete gap for a production-only crash if `SpansBuffer` or its internals aren’t spawn-picklable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated isinstance-vs-hasattr documentation edit in CLAUDE.md is scope drift not traceable to this PR's stated intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes a CLAUDE.md documentation addition about using isinstance() vs hasattr() for unions (lines added under the prefetch_related section). The rest of the PR changes are about span flusher multiprocessing limits and related consumer/flusher/test updates. This CLAUDE.md change is unrelated to the functional changes shown in the code diff and thus is verifiable scope drift within this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int) has zero call sites; restart path calls _create_process_for_shards directly, leaving a misleading unused entry point

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher`, the new method `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added but the diff shows no call sites for it. Process restarts in `_ensure_processes_alive()` directly call `self._create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, and initialization uses `_create_processes()` / `_create_process_for_shards(...)`. This makes `_create_process_for_shard` an unused/misleading entry point (dead code) and a maintainability issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag-key typo: wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag} while other timers use "shard", splitting the metric surface and breaking per-shard queries for produce latency

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the `produce` timer uses `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` and `segment_size_bytes` uses `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, but `wait_produce` is emitted as `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This inconsistency creates a separate tag key for the same dimension, splitting the metric series and preventing consistent per-shard latency queries for `wait_produce` compared to the other flusher metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Mixed health-state granularity: self.stopped/current_drift are per-flusher while healthy_since/backpressure_since are per-process, leaving a half-migrated health model

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally shares `stopped` and `current_drift` across all flusher workers (created once in `__init__` and passed to every process/thread), while `healthy_since`/`backpressure_since` are explicitly migrated to per-process `multiprocessing.Value`s (`process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`) and are consistently used in `_ensure_processes_alive()` and `submit()`. The finding correctly observes different granularities, but the diff does not show this causing inconsistent logic or broken behavior; it appears to be a deliberate design choice rather than a “half-migrated” health model defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sequential join() with shared deadline means only the first process gets the full timeout and later processes are terminate()'d mid-flush, losing buffered segments

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, a single `deadline = time.time() + timeout` is shared across a *sequential* loop over `self.processes`. For each process, it waits only while `deadline > time.time()`, and then unconditionally calls `process.terminate()` (for multiprocessing processes) after the wait. This means if the first process consumes most/all of the timeout, later processes may get little/no wait time and be terminated immediately when reached, which is a real shutdown-semantics concern introduced by the multi-process change. However, the claim about definite “losing buffered segments” can’t be strictly verified from the diff (termination is forceful but whether it causes actual segment loss depends on broader guarantees), so this is better classified as an important review issue rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deletion of self.buffer forces redundant loops over self.buffers in get_memory_info and record_stored_segments, and future all-shards code must remember to loop N buffers

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the prior single `self.buffer` is no longer stored/used; instead per-process shard buffers are created and kept in `self.buffers` (see `_create_process_for_shards`). As a result, call sites that previously operated on one buffer now must loop over `self.buffers.values()` (e.g. `submit`: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info`: aggregating `memory_infos` by extending from each buffer). This is not a correctness defect in the diff, but it is a concrete maintainability/architecture concern: future "all shards" operations must remember to iterate all buffers and may duplicate logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comment claims per-shard health check but code only checks process-level process_healthy_since, misleading readers debugging shard-level hangs

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the hang detection uses only `self.process_healthy_since[process_index]` (a per-process timestamp) to decide `cause = "hang"`, yet the inline comment says `# Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy`. There is no per-shard health tracking in the diff—only a single `healthy_since` value per process is updated in `main()`—so the comment (and resulting per-shard metric emission) can mislead someone debugging shard-specific hangs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a fixed-wait race bandaid that can flake on slow CI runners

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, `time.sleep` is monkeypatched at the start to `lambda _: None` (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`), and the later `time.sleep(0.1)` call uses that patched function. So the diff does not introduce a real fixed 0.1s wait that could flake on slow CI; the sleep is effectively a no-op in this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default max_processes changes from 1 process to one process per shard, causing 20-40 flusher processes per consumer with no operator opt-in or rollout flag (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the default process count in `SpanFlusher`: `__init__` now sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, followed by `_create_processes()` which creates one process per `process_index`. If `max_processes` is not provided (and `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.flusher_processes` defaults to `None`), this results in `num_processes == len(assigned_shards)` (i.e., effectively one process per shard). While a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with default `1` is added, this diff does not show wiring that guarantees it is always passed into the factory, so the concern about an implicit default scaling up to many processes is diff-grounded as an ops/rollout risk rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In thread mode, hang restart never stops the old hung thread since process.kill() is guarded by isinstance check, leaking a thread and running duplicate pollers on the same shards (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, when a thread is considered unhealthy due to hang (`time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds`), it attempts to stop it only via `process.kill()` guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so the hung thread is not stopped/terminated. The code then unconditionally starts a replacement thread via `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, meaning the old thread can continue running and a new poller is started for the same shard set, leaking threads and risking duplicate flush/poll behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() performs one record_stored_segments() Redis round-trip per process-buffer instead of one, multiplying Redis calls N× with per-shard default; get_memory_info also double-counts used/available N times (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher to create one SpansBuffer per process/shard-group (`self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer`). In `submit()`, it now loops over all buffers and calls `buffer.record_stored_segments()` for each (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`), whereas previously there was a single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call. This is a concrete N× increase in whatever Redis work `record_stored_segments()` performs, and is a performance/COGS concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect. The "double-counts used/available" part is not strictly verifiable from the diff because we can't see whether `get_memory_info()` is per-shard/per-buffer vs global (summing could be correct if buffers are disjoint shard subsets).

adjudication_records.issue_text: wait_produce timer tagged with 'shards' while sibling metrics use 'shard', splitting dashboard aggregation dimensions (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the new metrics tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use the key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This will split aggregation dimensions for related flusher metrics (dashboards/alerts keyed on one tag won’t line up with the other).

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is dead code with no caller and will drift from the real restart path (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff introduces `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` which is not referenced anywhere else in the shown changes. The actual restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, so the singular helper is currently unused and could drift from the real restart logic over time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes 0 is falsy and silently becomes one-per-shard; negative values produce zero flusher processes while consumer still accepts spans into Redis, with no validation of non-positive values (P2)

adjudication.rationale: `--flusher-processes` is passed as `flusher_processes` into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes `0` silently fall back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (effectively one-per-shard), and there is no validation for non-positive values. For negative values, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative, leading to an empty `process_to_shards_map` and then a `KeyError` when distributing shards (`self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`), i.e., a real crash/incorrect behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restart overwrites buffers/processes slots without join()ing killed processes, accumulating un-reaped zombies under rapid crash-restart cycles (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, unhealthy `multiprocessing.Process` instances are `kill()`ed and then immediately replaced via `_create_process_for_shards`, which overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` with the new process. The old `Process` object is not `join()`ed (or otherwise reaped) before its reference is lost, and `join()` later only waits on the *current* entries in `self.processes`. Under repeated crash/restart, this can leave terminated child processes unreaped (zombies on POSIX) because the parent never joins them once overwritten.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shard assignment is fixed at construction; a caller that constructs once and rebalances in place gets shards no process polls, stalling data in Redis (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `process_to_shards_map` and per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances are derived once from `buffer.assigned_shards` and then reused (`self.buffers[...] = shard_buffer`). There is no code in this diff that updates the shard->process mapping or recreates buffers/processes when shard assignments change later. If the consumer can rebalance partitions without reconstructing the flusher/strategy, newly assigned shards would not be polled by any existing process, potentially leaving data in Redis. The diff alone doesn’t prove that such in-place rebalancing happens, so it’s a grounded edge-case/architecture concern rather than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit never runs messages through the processes, so shared-shard flush behavior and multi-process restart path are unexercised and regressions pass green (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the test only creates the strategy with 4 partitions and asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2` plus shard distribution, then immediately `step.join()` without ever calling `step.submit(...)` or otherwise causing any spans/segments to be buffered and flushed. Because it passes `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, `SpanFlusher` uses `threading.Thread` (not `multiprocessing.Process`) in `_create_process_for_shards`, so the multi-process behavior and shared-shard flush behavior are not exercised. Likewise, the restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive()` is never triggered. This is a concrete coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS circuit breaker converted from a consumer-wide cap to a per-process budget, multiplying the crash-loop alarm threshold by the number of processes (e.g., 32×) and letting a flapping process never trip the consumer restart

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes restart accounting from a single `self.process_restarts` counter to a per-process dictionary: `self.process_restarts = {process_index: 0 ...}` and the circuit-break check is now `if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise ...` inside the per-process loop in `_ensure_processes_alive()`. This does increase the *aggregate* number of flusher restarts the consumer can tolerate (roughly `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` per process) before forcing a consumer restart, which could weaken the intended “consumer-level” crash-loop breaker. However, the finding’s claim that a single flapping process would “never trip” is not supported: a repeatedly failing process still increments its own counter and will eventually raise once it exceeds `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The join loop breaks out entirely once remaining_time <= 0, so processes after the currently-waited one never get terminate() called, leaking flusher processes holding Redis connections and Kafka producers past shutdown

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes` does `if remaining_time <= 0: break`, which exits the entire loop before reaching later processes. Since `process.terminate()` is only called inside that loop after waiting on each process, any processes after the break will not be terminated and may remain alive past shutdown. This is directly shown in the new join implementation in `flusher.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key drift: timers use tag 'shard' while wait_produce uses 'shards', splitting one logical metric family across two tag keys and breaking dashboards/alerts

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the metrics timers use inconsistent tag keys for the same shard identifier: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `"shards"`. This will split metric series/dashboards/alerts by two different tag keys for the same logical dimension. It’s an instrumentation/observability issue rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) makes --flusher-processes 0 silently spawn one process per shard (the maximum), contradicting the CLI help text and operator intent

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy, so a CLI value of `--flusher-processes 0` results in `max_processes` becoming `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. Then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` spawns one process per shard (the maximum). The new Click option (`type=int`, no bounds) allows `0`, so this is a real, diff-grounded behavioral defect that contradicts the option’s intent as a cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_basic converted to django_db(transaction=True) with a bare time.sleep(0.1) that is not a synchronization mechanism, making the test intermittently fail or silently pass on stale/empty output

adjudication.rationale: In `test_basic`, the test still does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, and the new `time.sleep(0.1)` (added after `step.poll()`) calls that patched `time.sleep`, so it provides no real waiting/synchronization. If the intent is to let the flusher thread/process do work before assertions, this is an ineffective (and generally brittle) sync approach. The finding’s “silently pass on stale/empty output” is not directly supported (the test asserts on produced messages), but the synchronization concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shards replaces self.buffers[process_index] with a new SpansBuffer without teardown of the old one, leaking Redis connection pool handles and losing unflushed segment bookkeeping on restarts

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, each restart constructs a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` and then overwrites `self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer` without any explicit teardown/close of the prior buffer object. The diff shows the old buffer reference is dropped, so if `SpansBuffer` owns external resources (e.g., Redis client/pool handles) or in-memory bookkeeping, that state would be discarded on restart. However, the diff does not show `SpansBuffer`’s internals, so the claim about Redis pool handle leakage and specific “unflushed segment bookkeeping” loss cannot be definitively verified from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-process backpressure semantics have defects

adjudication.rationale: The new backpressure tracking is per-process (`process_backpressure_since`), but `SpanFlusher.submit()` applies it globally: it iterates over *all* `process_backpressure_since` values and raises `MessageRejected()` if **any** process has been backpressured longer than the threshold. This means one slow/stuck shard group can reject ingestion for unrelated shards handled by other processes, since submit does not correlate the incoming message/shard to a specific process/shard group. That’s a potentially unintended/overly aggressive semantic change introduced by the multi-process refactor, but it’s not a clearly verifiable correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restart-counter behavior is incorrect

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes restart tracking from a single `self.process_restarts` counter to a per-process dict (`self.process_restarts[process_index]`), and it is still incremented only when an unhealthy process is detected. The guard (`if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise`) is the same pattern as before (previously `if self.process_restarts > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`). From the diff alone, there’s no clear evidence that the restart-counter logic is now incorrect or that it regressed vs. prior behavior; any off-by-one interpretation would apply equally to the old code and isn’t verifiably wrong without additional spec/context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `join` deadline handling is problematic

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, deadline handling can leave some child processes unhandled. The loop breaks early when `remaining_time <= 0` (computed but otherwise unused), which stops iterating over the rest of `self.processes`; any remaining processes after the break are neither waited on nor terminated. Previously (single `self.process`) the code always reached a termination step; now timeout can prevent cleanup of later processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call replaced by per-shard buffers raises correctness/architecture concerns

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove `record_stored_segments()`; it changes `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to a loop calling `buffer.record_stored_segments()` for each per-process/per-shard `SpansBuffer` stored in `self.buffers` (see `submit`). The finding’s premise (“Removed … call”) misreads the change, and the rest is a vague concern not tied to a specific, verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts internal structure (process counts, shard sums) mirroring constructor arithmetic, and never asserts messages or commits after step.join(), so a completely broken shared-process flusher still passes

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, after `step = fac.create_with_partitions(...)` the test only checks internal fields on `fac._flusher` (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and that `process_to_shards_map` covers 4 shards). It never drives the flusher to actually flush/produce spans or asserts any effects such as `messages` being produced or `commits` being recorded before/after `step.join()`. Since the new logic in `SpanFlusher` is about running shared processes per shard set and producing to Kafka, a flusher that misbehaves at runtime could still satisfy these constructor-derived invariants and pass this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_basic only runs with default flusher_processes=None, so the multi-process code path is never exercised against real data

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s implication doesn’t follow from the diff. `flusher_processes=None` does not force a single flusher worker: `SpanFlusher.__init__` sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, so the default can still create multiple workers when multiple shards are assigned. Additionally, the new `test_flusher_processes_limit` explicitly sets `flusher_processes=2` and asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, exercising the multi-worker mapping/creation logic. Whether `test_basic` uses >1 partition isn’t shown, so the claim that multi-worker code is “never exercised” is not verifiable from this diff and is contradicted by the new test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _ensure_processes_alive health monitoring logic has zero test coverage: no test kills a process, manipulates process_healthy_since, or drives the restart loop (including MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, kill/already-closed path, and restart via _create_process_for_shards)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new multi-process health monitoring and restart logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive()` (checks `process.is_alive()`, checks `process_healthy_since[...]` vs `max-unhealthy-seconds`, increments `process_restarts[...]`, attempts `process.kill()` with exception handling, and restarts via `_create_process_for_shards`). The added/updated tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the `process_backpressure_since` assertion change) only validate basic flushing, process count/shard distribution, and backpressure flagging; none kill a process, force an unhealthy `process_healthy_since` to trigger a hang, exercise the kill/already-closed exception path, or drive the `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError branch. This is a specific, diff-grounded lack of coverage for newly added nontrivial behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() lets the first slow process consume the entire shared deadline, breaking the outer loop and leaving remaining processes neither joined nor terminate()d (leaked processes holding Redis connections); no test calls join with a timeout on a multi-process flusher

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, a shared `deadline` is computed once, then the method iterates processes. If the first `process` stays alive until the deadline passes, the next loop iteration computes `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` and `break`s the `for` loop when `remaining_time <= 0` (new code in `join`). That exits without joining/terminating the remaining processes, leaving them running. This behavior is newly relevant with `self.processes` (multi-process flusher) introduced in this diff. The added tests only call `step.join()` with no timeout, so there is no coverage for `join(timeout=...)` on a multi-process flusher.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard (singular) is dead code with no call site anywhere in the diff; restart path calls _create_process_for_shards (plural), so it silently never executes — deletion candidate

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff introduces `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` but no code shown in this diff calls it. The actual restart/health-check path in `_ensure_processes_alive` restarts via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, so the singular helper appears unused within the changed code and is a reasonable cleanup/deletion candidate. However, this is a maintainability issue (potential dead code), not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone since there could be external call sites outside the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weakened assertion at test_flusher.py:83 uses any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values()), which passes if any process is in backpressure rather than the specific tested process, masking per-process backpressure state

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the flusher from a single backpressure flag (`flusher.backpressure_since.value`) to per-process flags (`flusher.process_backpressure_since`). The updated test assertion in `test_flusher.py` now checks `any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())`, which is a weaker condition if multiple processes/threads exist, because it no longer verifies backpressure state for a particular expected process/shard mapping—only that at least one process hit backpressure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() backpressure semantics changed (raises MessageRejected if any per-process value exceeds threshold), but no test verifies that submit raises MessageRejected after the threshold elapses

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SpanFlusher.submit()` backpressure handling from a single `self.backpressure_since` to iterating all `self.process_backpressure_since` values and raising `MessageRejected` if *any* process has been backpressured longer than `backpressure_secs` (see `for backpressure_since in self.process_backpressure_since.values(): ... raise MessageRejected()`). The updated/added tests only assert that some backpressure flag is set (`test_flusher.py` now checks `any(x.value ...)`) and do not verify the time-threshold behavior or that `submit()` raises `MessageRejected` after the threshold elapses under the new per-process model. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for newly introduced nontrivial logic, not a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hang-restart in thread mode (produce_to_pipe non-None) leaks the hung thread and spawns a second concurrent flusher for the same shards, since the caught (ValueError, AttributeError) path calls _create_process_for_shards without a per-process stop flag

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (see `make_process = threading.Thread`) and passes the shared `self.stopped` flag to `main`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, on hang it only attempts `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`; for threads it does nothing (caught `(ValueError, AttributeError)`), then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. That spawns a new thread for the same shard set without stopping the old hung thread (no per-thread stop flag is set), so you can end up with multiple concurrent flushers for the same shards and a leaked hung thread.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Killed/replaced processes are never join()ed in _ensure_processes_alive, accumulating zombie SpawnProcess entries (holding pickled SpansBuffer/pipe resources) across repeated crash-restart cycles

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, unhealthy processes are restarted by calling `process.kill()` (only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`) and then `_create_process_for_shards(...)` to start a replacement, but the killed/replaced `multiprocessing.Process` is never `join()`ed/cleaned up before being overwritten in `self.processes[process_index]` (`_create_process_for_shards` assigns `self.processes[process_index] = process`). This diff shows no join/close path during restart (only in `join()` at shutdown), so repeated crash-restart cycles can leave terminated children unreaped (zombie) and leak resources. Additionally, in the thread-based path (`produce_to_pipe` not None), the restart logic does not stop the old thread at all (it only kills multiprocessing.Process), so restarts on `cause == "hang"` would create additional live threads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag-key inconsistency: the wait_produce timer uses tag key "shards" while flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes use "shard", splitting the metric series and making produce-wait latency invisible to existing dashboards

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main` the metrics tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use tag key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This will split series by tag key and can break/fragment existing dashboards and alerts that expect a consistent tag schema, but it doesn't directly break runtime correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is a dead method with a misleading contract — it restarts an entire process group rather than one shard and has no callers

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is newly added but there are no call sites in the diff (the code paths use `_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive`). Additionally, despite its name/contract (“for_shard”), it restarts the entire process handling that shard by calling `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` for the full shard group, which is potentially misleading for future maintainers. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability concern, but not a runtime defect given it’s unused.

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher_processes=0 (or negative) silently means one process per shard (the maximum) instead of an error, inverting the intent of operators setting 0

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses truthiness. If `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is passed as `0`, it is falsy and gets replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, effectively enabling the maximum (one process per shard) silently, which inverts the intent of setting 0. (Negative values don’t map to max; they would lead to invalid `self.num_processes` and likely crash later.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-message Redis call amplification in flusher submit(): loop issues one Redis round-trip set per flusher process, plus get_memory_info() per buffer when max-memory-percentage < 1.0, all on the consumer's hot ingest path; with N processes this multiplies synchronous Redis traffic and can itself trigger MessageRejected under backpressure

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()` the diff changes from a single `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` call to looping over `self.buffers.values()` and calling `record_stored_segments()` once per flusher subprocess (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`). Likewise, when `max_memory_percentage < 1.0`, it now aggregates `memory_infos` by calling `buffer.get_memory_info()` for every buffer/process. If those methods hit Redis (not shown here, but implied by the flusher/buffer design), this change can multiply synchronous Redis work per submitted message as the number of flusher processes increases. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded scalability/perf concern on the consumer’s per-message path, but not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Empty assigned_shards at construction makes num_processes 0, silently disabling the flusher entirely: no process polls Redis, spans rot in Redis while offsets are still committed, with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. If `buffer.assigned_shards` is empty, `len(...)` is 0, so `num_processes` becomes 0, `process_to_shards_map`/`processes` stay empty, and `_create_processes()` starts nothing. Later `submit()` calls `_ensure_processes_alive()` but it iterates over `self.processes.items()` (empty), so no error is surfaced and nothing polls Redis. This “no shards => no flusher process” behavior is visible in the diff and is a regression from the prior single-process `_create_process()` logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is a dead-but-dangerous restart helper that doesn't kill the old process, doesn't increment process_restarts, and bypasses the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS check, risking zombie processes and unbounded restart loops if wired in

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` a helper `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` was added that finds the owning `process_index` and calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly. Unlike the real restart path in `_ensure_processes_alive`, it does not (a) kill/terminate the existing process for that `process_index`, (b) increment `self.process_restarts[process_index]`, or (c) enforce `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`. Since `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new process and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]`, this would orphan the old process if the helper were ever used. The diff does not show it being called, so it’s not a currently-triggered defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded footgun.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag key for the same dimension: 'spans.buffer.flusher.produce' uses tag 'shard' while 'spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce' uses 'shards', splitting dashboards/alerts into disjoint series and breaking series continuity

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an inconsistent tag key for what appears to be the same shard-dimension: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` vs `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` in `SpanFlusher.main`. This will split metrics into different tag sets/series, which can disrupt dashboards/alerts and series continuity, but it’s an observability/consistency issue rather than a direct runtime correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: shard_tag joins all shard ids into a comma-separated metric tag value (e.g. '0,1,2,...,63') when one process covers many shards, causing metric cardinality blowup and making per-shard breakdowns structurally impossible

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, `shard_tag` is computed as `",".join(map(str, shards))` and then used as a metrics tag value (e.g. `metrics.timer(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`). When a process handles multiple shards (which this diff explicitly enables via `process_to_shards_map` and `max_processes` limiting), the tag becomes a shard-set string like `"0,1,2,3"`. That makes the tag value depend on shard grouping/assignment rather than a single shard, which can increase tag cardinality and prevents true per-shard breakdowns from these metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes 0 (or falsy value) is silently converted via `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` to one process per shard (the maximum) rather than being rejected or clamped, causing silent maximal process fan-out

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` (or any falsy int) as “unset” and silently replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (one process per shard). Since the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no min/clamp, a user can pass `0` and unexpectedly trigger maximal process fan-out rather than getting an error or a 0/1-process behavior.
